nodes.Name: processStatus
nodes.DocComment: processStatus describes the status of a [Process].

nodes.Name: Process
nodes.DocComment: Process stores the information about a process created by [StartProcess].

Fields.Name: sigMu
Fields.DocComment: avoid race between wait and signal

nodes.Name: processHandle
nodes.DocComment:
processHandle holds an operating system handle to a process.
This is only used on systems that support that concept,
currently Linux and Windows.
This maintains a reference count to the handle,
and closes the handle when the reference drops to zero.

nodes.Name: acquire
nodes.DocComment:
acquire adds a reference and returns the handle.
The bool result reports whether acquire succeeded;
it fails if the handle is already closed.
Every successful call to acquire should be paired with a call to release.

nodes.Name: release
nodes.DocComment: release releases a reference to the handle.

nodes.Name: newPIDProcess
nodes.DocComment: newPIDProcess returns a [Process] for the given PID.

nodes.Name: newHandleProcess
nodes.DocComment: newHandleProcess returns a [Process] with the given PID and handle.

nodes.Name: newDoneProcess
nodes.DocComment:
newDoneProcess returns a [Process] for the given PID
that is already marked as done. This is used on Unix systems
if the process is known to not exist.

nodes.Name: handleTransientAcquire
nodes.DocComment:
handleTransientAcquire returns the process handle or,
if the process is not ready, the current status.

nodes.Name: handleTransientRelease
nodes.DocComment: handleTransientRelease releases a handle returned by handleTransientAcquire.

nodes.Name: pidStatus
nodes.DocComment: pidStatus returns the current process status.

nodes.Name: ProcAttr
nodes.DocComment:
ProcAttr holds the attributes that will be applied to a new process
started by StartProcess.

nodes.Name: Signal
nodes.DocComment:
A Signal represents an operating system signal.
The usual underlying implementation is operating system-dependent:
on Unix it is syscall.Signal.

nodes.Name: Getpid
nodes.DocComment: Getpid returns the process id of the caller.

nodes.Name: Getppid
nodes.DocComment: Getppid returns the process id of the caller's parent.

nodes.Name: FindProcess
nodes.DocComment:
FindProcess looks for a running process by its pid.

The [Process] it returns can be used to obtain information
about the underlying operating system process.

On Unix systems, FindProcess always succeeds and returns a Process
for the given pid, regardless of whether the process exists. To test whether
the process actually exists, see whether p.Signal(syscall.Signal(0)) reports
an error.

nodes.Name: StartProcess
nodes.DocComment:
StartProcess starts a new process with the program, arguments and attributes
specified by name, argv and attr. The argv slice will become [os.Args] in the
new process, so it normally starts with the program name.

If the calling goroutine has locked the operating system thread
with [runtime.LockOSThread] and modified any inheritable OS-level
thread state (for example, Linux or Plan 9 name spaces), the new
process will inherit the caller's thread state.

StartProcess is a low-level interface. The [os/exec] package provides
higher-level interfaces.

If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

nodes.Name: Release
nodes.DocComment:
Release releases any resources associated with the [Process] p,
rendering it unusable in the future.
Release only needs to be called if [Process.Wait] is not.

nodes.Name: doRelease
nodes.DocComment:
doRelease releases a [Process], setting the status to newStatus.
If the previous status is not statusOK, this does nothing.
It returns the previous status.

nodes.Name: Kill
nodes.DocComment:
Kill causes the [Process] to exit immediately. Kill does not wait until
the Process has actually exited. This only kills the Process itself,
not any other processes it may have started.

nodes.Name: Wait
nodes.DocComment:
Wait waits for the [Process] to exit, and then returns a
ProcessState describing its status and an error, if any.
Wait releases any resources associated with the Process.
On most operating systems, the Process must be a child
of the current process or an error will be returned.

nodes.Name: Signal
nodes.DocComment:
Signal sends a signal to the [Process].
Sending [Interrupt] on Windows is not implemented.

nodes.Name: WithHandle
nodes.DocComment:
WithHandle calls a supplied function f with a valid process handle
as an argument. The handle is guaranteed to refer to process p
until f returns, even if p terminates. This function cannot be used
after [Process.Release] or [Process.Wait].

If process handles are not supported or a handle is not available,
it returns [ErrNoHandle]. Currently, process handles are supported
on Linux 5.4 or later (pidfd) and Windows.

nodes.Name: UserTime
nodes.DocComment: UserTime returns the user CPU time of the exited process and its children.

nodes.Name: SystemTime
nodes.DocComment: SystemTime returns the system CPU time of the exited process and its children.

nodes.Name: Exited
nodes.DocComment:
Exited reports whether the program has exited.
On Unix systems this reports true if the program exited due to calling exit,
but false if the program terminated due to a signal.

nodes.Name: Success
nodes.DocComment:
Success reports whether the program exited successfully,
such as with exit status 0 on Unix.

nodes.Name: Sys
nodes.DocComment:
Sys returns system-dependent exit information about
the process. Convert it to the appropriate underlying
type, such as [syscall.WaitStatus] on Unix, to access its contents.

nodes.Name: SysUsage
nodes.DocComment:
SysUsage returns system-dependent resource usage information about
the exited process. Convert it to the appropriate underlying
type, such as [*syscall.Rusage] on Unix, to access its contents.
(On Unix, *syscall.Rusage matches struct rusage as defined in the
getrusage(2) manual page.)
